title: Information Systems Manager (I) (LtCol to 2ndLt) FMOS, DIR C4
raw_text:
14.     MOS 8848, Information Systems Manager (I) (LtCol to 2ndLt) FMOS, DIR C4

    a. Summary. Management, Data Systems Officers, manage system
development activities, including assessment of feasibility, detailed system
design, testing, conversion, implementation, and post-implementation review.

       b.   Prerequisites.   Must be an unrestricted officer.

    c. Requirements. Complete the Information Technology Management
Curriculum Number 370 at the Naval Postgraduate School, Monterey, CA or
equivalent postgraduate degree from an accredited institution.

       d.   Duties

        (1) Determines the need for the integration of existing and
developing systems.

        (2) Coordinates ADP management policy with technical management,
functional management, and senior ADP policy officials.

        (3) Coordinates the development of measurable objectives for system
performance that form the baseline for the measurement of system
effectiveness.

        (4) Specifies and coordinates current hardware, software, and project
management practices for both the technical and user systems development
staff.

        (5) Determines management strategy, policy, and doctrine for system
development, documentation, and information processing management standards.

        (6) Conducts evaluation of existing information systems with regard
to throughput performance, utilization of input/output media, and overall
user satisfaction.

        (7) Participates in the evaluation of system development
documentation to ensure economic and operational viability of the system,
integrity of system design, and understanding of the system by both
functional managers and the technical systems staff.




                                         1-356                      Enclosure (1)
 1147                                                                  NAVMC 1200.1L



       e.   Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code

            (1) Computer Hardware Engineers 17-2061.

            (2) Computer and Information Systems Managers 11-3021.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   None.

(2) Coordinates ADP management policy with technical management, functional management, and senior ADP policy officials.

Confer with staff, users, and management to establish requirements for new systems or modifications.
(4) Specifies and coordinates current hardware, software, and project management practices for both the technical and user systems development staff.
Develop, document, or maintain standards, best practices, or system usage procedures.
(5) Determines management strategy, policy, and doctrine for system development, documentation, and information processing management standards.
Evaluate existing systems to determine effectiveness, and suggest changes to meet organizational requirements.
(6) Conducts evaluation of existing information systems with regard to throughput performance, utilization of input/output media, and overall user satisfaction.
Develop or direct software system testing or validation procedures, programming, or documentation.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
